column1: # DUMMY FILE for the demo: reviewer DEMO-A is fictional; these codes were written to illustrate the format

column2: It is fast at boilerplate, but the code it writes ignores our team's naming conventions.
Explaining legacy code is the best part. It summarised a 600-line function in plain English.
Sometimes it invents API methods that do not exist, and I lose time chasing them.
I finish routine tickets faster, so I have more time for design work.
column3: faster routine work; time for design

column2: It helped me pick up Rust much faster than reading the book alone.
Pair programming with it feels like working with a fast but careless intern.
I use it to write documentation comments. It turns my notes into readable docstrings.
It is good at explaining error messages and suggesting what to try next.
